page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the n4 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel processor features a cache hierarchy consisting of a 48 KB L1d cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a substantial 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512f, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for accelerated matrix operations. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI flags, alongside integer and bit manipulation features like BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1561.99 and Geekbench single-core reaching 1807.0, both falling in the average tier. Single-threaded gzip compression (28.23 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (12.03 GB/sec) also demonstrate average throughput. However, multi-core and memory-bound metrics are relatively weak. The Geekbench multi-core score of 4100.0, the Passmark CPU score of 6010.98, and the Redis SET throughput of 4.62 million operations per second fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with uncached large-block reads at 32.36 GB/sec and writes at 21.01 GB/sec.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the n4-standard-4 is positioned as a cost-efficient general-purpose instance for workloads that do not demand sustained multi-core execution or high memory bandwidth. It is well-suited for static web serving, where it achieves an average throughput of 6.53 GB/sec, as well as light text processing and basic single-threaded applications. It can also handle lightweight, small-scale LLM text generation, though it is less optimal for intensive compilation, database operations, or multi-threaded decompression tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-4 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated Intel vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyper-threading) and 16.0 GB of RAM. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. Performance benchmarks show average single-core execution, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1807.0 and static web serving throughput of 6.53 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations, such as Redis SET and software compilation, perform in the lower tier. Qualitatively, the n4-standard-4 offers a balanced resource profile for entry-level general-purpose workloads, making it suitable for static web serving, light text processing, and basic single-threaded applications that do not require high memory bandwidth or sustained multi-threaded compute.
